claims.claim: Combat against the Typhon enemies reveals limitations quickly, and the opening hours feel difficult or punishing for players with slower reflexes.

citations.review_text:
I love immersive sims, and I'm sure Prey is a good game.

However, after a strong start, my enthusiasm quickly faded. There's a lot of looting for crafting materials, a mechanic I despise. The combat against the Typhon, after the first few encounters, already shows its limitations. There's barely any stealth. The environment feels sterile and devoid of life.

The best immsim, Deus Ex, has tons of moments where you interact with civilians, whole levels built around nothing but exploration and social encounters, and a huge variety of environments. There's none of that here. You have no one to interact with, the story is slowly drip-fed to you through radio and documents, and you're just running around a single hostile place. I can't help feeling that Bioshock did it better, many years ago.
Premise is interesting. World is pretty. Combat is annoying enough that I can't justify more playtime. If you have older hands and reflexes, I recommend steering clear.

This game is not for the casual gamer who lacks the reflexes and free time of the young. I've only made it as far as the lobby level, and am now giving up after reading up on how the game is meant to be hardcore, even on the easiest mode.

I picked this up on a sale based on hearing that it was an underrated gem, which it might be. At this point, I'd have to watch someone else play this on youtube or something. Please enjoy this game if it's your thing, but us oldsters who can't keep up should probably pass on this.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience controller detection issues, noting that controllers do not work upon launch despite advertised full support.

citations.review_text: Why does this game list controller support? Bought years ago but just tired to play for the first time, probably spent an hour trying to get it to detect my controller.  In 13 years of PC gaming this is the first steam game that listed full controller support that didn't just work upon launching the game.

I have no clue how this game is rated so high.  There's no support for controller or MOUSE!?

Refunded.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the GLOO cannon can be used to bypass various environmental obstacles and reach locked areas.

citations.review_text:
do give a lot of praise for not hand holding my way through the game with objectives but a lot of problems can just be solved by using the gloo cannon. actually, most of them can, compounded by the fact you can just invest in jump height. 

Fire blocking your way? Gloo. 
Too many enemies in a room or you need to escape? Gloo.
Cystoid nests in your way? Gloo.
Getting to a room without a code or around a group of enemies? Gloo staircase and smashing through the window.
Electric arcs in your way? Gloo.
One of the cheapest and first ammo types you unlock in the game? Gloo.
Platform you need to get to? Gloo.
Technopath you HAVE to kill to get through a locked door? Gloo.

The only time Gloo could NOT solve a problem was radiation. but theres no radiation suit or anything so all of the leaking barrels are placed in spots you can just walk around or completely avoid.
In the uncommon case you cant just get into a room by using Gloo, it could be solved by spending, one or two neuromods on mimic matter. Congratulations, almost every locked door, room or puzzle can be solved with one of those two things.

Its an interesting problem, they show you multiple times in the game that you can use gloo to solve problems easily. and then when i realized that i could just, solve all of my problems with one weapon and one power, the game became really boring. Why would i search for an alternate solution if i can just use the far more convient and faster method of becoming a coffee cup or binder and slipping through a gap in the window, or building a stair case using the cheapest ammunition in the game. 

For a game that recieves a lot of praise for "making you think" It really only boiled down to two decisions for me.

Oh man, if you want a game similar to Bioshock and System Shock with a bit of Alien Isolation thrown in, this is it. You can solve environmental puzzles in so many unique ways. You may think you are stuck in some parts, but you aren't. You can get out of all situations with just playing around with the mechanics. It may not seem like it at first, but your choices in the game matter, but the world is so living that these choices weigh heavy. I wish on my first playthrough I realized this...there are moments when you may be locked out of a questline because some do expire. Take your time and explore, it seems scary at first but you will frequently circle around the same areas so often that you will know how to get around.

Definitely get this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening section and early hours as tedious or frustrating due to searching for enemies disguised as everyday objects.

citations.review_text:
For me, this game feels like a chore to play.

The whole opening of this game is walking around an abandoned facility, reading emails and collecting garbage to recycle.
The story isn't also introduced very well in my opinion.

The combat is centred around mimic monsters hiding as an item in the environment. Searching around an office for a monster posing as a coffee cup is just tedious as hell.

I haven't played this game for very long but it's lost my interest QUICKLY.

Pros: 
Interesting setting

Solid art direction

Engaging story and extremely detailed world (so many little easter eggs and bits of lore to find!) Lots of weapon and item variety

Side missions that actually take advantage of backtracking in an interesting way

Actually did a cool [spoiler]“it was all a simulation” ending [/spoiler]

When it works, it works well

Cons:
Frustrating intro and first 2 hours, especially with how abundant mimics are before you get the scanner.

Feels like stealth should be an option, but it often isn’t. Almost never gives you the freedom to do important tasks in stealth, and enemy sightlines feel inconsistent and unpredictable.

Some really annoying encounters like the nightmare, who you need to just wait out, and telepaths who have awful pathfinding, a symptom of the overall terrible ai. Not to mention respawning enemies. 

It’s fine that combat is difficult, but you feel much more sluggish than your enemies made worse by how buggy weapon switching can be.

Feels like a significant step back from dishonored, and actually gives you less freedom in enemy encounters despite the open-ended map and abundance of weapons and items.

All of the fun powers are locked behind a path that has massive drawbacks and makes you have to deal with tedious enemy encounters more consistently.

Some great high moments, but the low moments make it feel like a slog.

It did some things great. But I can't get over it's shortcomings, especially when contrasted with Arkane's other works.

citations.review_text: 7/10 - Definitely a good game with a lot of effort put into it. Trademark "Arcane" exploration opportunities are as impressive as in dishonored if not more. Personally i struggled to enjoy recycling gameplay loop which got old fast. Also enemies i found quite irritating, not fun to fight against. Which resulted in me to run away from them. Which resulted in reduced ability to explore and care about what's going on.

First time I played this game was years ago and I put about 10 hours into it. Thought I'd give it a new try and see what I think of it now.

It's still ass and makes me want to play Dishonored instead. I was already getting pissed off about two hours in this time. Started running and gunning to see how far I could get before the game either gets good or I ragequit. I ragequit about two hours later.

I remember now that I hated the Mimics. I still do. Such a stupid and annoying design for an enemy. "Look for dublicate objects or something that's out of place". Yeah, I did. In every room and in every one of them there are dublicate objects or something out of place so I still have to go swinging in with my wrench and check if there's a Mimic hiding in there. And in so many places there are. This would be somewhat more tolerable if the main character did not have a stamina bar, but of course s/he does! And you run out of stamina so fast too, at least without any upgrades, but who would upgrade their stamina when there's much more useful and fun things to unlock?

Why does the mouse sensitivity change when the character sprints? This shouldn't be a thing.

If you want to be more effective in combat, you have to use the GLOO gun first and then switch into something else. But of course the weapon switching is slow and delayed as well.

I managed to find 3 different enemies and none of them felt satisfying to fight against. One of the reasons being the weapons that are very inaccurate when you try hitting anything more than 2 meters away. There's no aiming down sights in this game.

Oh and if the enemies hurt you, you can heal yourself infinitely... By drinking from water fountains one button tap at a time. It will heal for 1hp and there's a cooldown of about 3 seconds before you can use it again. Thanks for making me waste time. Sure, I could eat the food I've collected, but those could also be recycled and turned into crafting materials.

Verdict on the game? It's frustr…

citations.review_text:
I’m still playing Prey, but so far I’m seriously impressed with it. The atmosphere on Talos I is incredible, and the constant feeling that something could be waiting around the corner keeps the game exciting.

I really enjoy the freedom the game gives you, whether it’s exploring, solving problems, fighting enemies, or finding creative ways around obstacles. The story and world-building are also keeping me interested and making me want to explore every part of the station.

I haven’t finished it yet, so I’m saving my final verdict for later, but after the time I’ve put in so far, I can already say this is a fantastic immersive-sim experience. Definitely worth playing if you’re a fan of Arkane’s games.

Prey is soooooo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I think it's an absolute masterpiece in the immersive sim genre, and probably Arkane Studios' magnum opus. 

Initially, I picked it up expecting something like Bioshock, but the depth of the gameplay and story was far deeper than I had expected. In basically every part of the game, from combat encounters to hacking a computer. there are always probably at least three ways to solve a problem. For example, At one point in the game, you have to shut off Talos I's fusion reactor and restart it in order to reboot the station's computer system. After restarting it, you have to replace a broken piece of the reactor. There are several ways of doing this: you can find a replacement part in the general area around the reactor behind a locked door, explore the area to find the part in a hidden area, or fix the broken part yourself if your character is skilled enough in repair to do so. All of the characters in the game are accounted for by the environment of Talos I, and feel like real people. Every corpse you encounter on the station has a designated workplace somewhere in the station, a bunk, a computer, etc. For a game that performed very poorly at its launch and that is hardly ever discussed online anymore, it's an astonishing amount of detail. 

The opening of the game had me hooked from the start. The moment I found out that Morgan's apartment was fake and broke open its windows was probably the coolest moment I've ever experienced in any video game. 

Admittedly, here are some things I disliked. The enemy selection is pretty poor. Until the last three or so hours of the game, basically every enemy you fight is the same alien creature crammed into a different body shape. The game could use more weapons. You're limited to about ten weapons (guns, grenades, etc.) total, not including neuromod abilities. And most of them (e.g., the Disruptor) are too niche to be useful in most situations. Yo, no joke. I'mma be real. This is one of the best games I've ever played. It's a mix of Deus Ex and Bioshock, but set in a space station. There are multiple ways to get around the map depending on the skills you choose and multiple options to solve issues or puzzles in the game. The story is engaging and interesting. The world is mysterious and thought-provoking. The characters are memorable. The graphics are beautiful. The soundtrack is incredible. I wish there was any chance at all of this game getting a sequel. It's truly a gem of a game. Grab it on sale if you need to, just give it a shot. It’s so worth it. 10/10

Note: My steam hours are not reflective of the amount of time I put into this game. I have over 200 hours on the PS4. I purchased it again on Steam because I wanted to play it on better hardware.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the opening hours involve considerable time reading emails, listening to audio logs, and searching environments.

citations.review_text:
For me, this game feels like a chore to play.

The whole opening of this game is walking around an abandoned facility, reading emails and collecting garbage to recycle.
The story isn't also introduced very well in my opinion.

The combat is centred around mimic monsters hiding as an item in the environment. Searching around an office for a monster posing as a coffee cup is just tedious as hell.

I haven't played this game for very long but it's lost my interest QUICKLY.

Highly recommend Prey. It’s a fantastic psychological thriller where you spend the first 5 hours hitting coffee mugs, chairs, and toilet paper rolls with a wrench just to make sure they won't try to eat your face.

Cool concept. Great world and atmosphere. Talos I is seriously an awesome setting for a game and its clear the devs focused on this. Typhons are a good balance between something new, but still rooted in familiarity for enemy types. The world building is truly one of the only highlights of this game. Talos I genuinely feels like it could be built in a real scenario. The organization of the departments and overall architecture is all very sound to how laymen would understand what "realistic" sci-fi could look like.

Onto the rest... The story is uninteresting, riddled with middling writing overall. I listened to most of the audio logs (even when they had to repeat themselves over and over again due to overlapping npcs and events occurring), as well as read most emails. People boast about how much of an immersive sim this game is, but realistically, Prey is still pretty linear. They do give you workarounds into other pathways and departments, access to some power resources and guns in multiple ways. But, the questing is all very much linear. You don't really get rewarded for exploring things "out of order" and the game forces you to backtrack anyways like a Metroidvania would. Timed quests are a cool concept, mixed execution. Grabbing the pills to save your coworker vs "protecting your brother in his bunker". When they introduce the protecting your brother objective, they don't really allude to it being a heavily pressing matter. They also drop like 5 other objectives for you, one which is to shutdown the hacking robot that is causing enemy spam across the whole ship. It was just an obnoxious implementation all around. Grabbing the pills was completely optional, but allowed the freedom to explore some side story and character connections you only would've been hinted at through a couple files and emails throughout the game. The character would've died without them and they played a somewhat important role. 

The first half of the game is focused on the "immersive" part…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily reliant on backtracking and traversing previously visited zones, particularly as the story progresses.

citations.review_text: Incredibly immersive and a memorable experience. The gameplay and different weapons are fun and traversing the ship is enjoyable. You are sometimes going back over yourself multiple times but this is kept interesting by things changing.

I have a mixed opinion. I enjoyed gameplay and was scared in the beginning a lot. But unfortunately it started to be too clanky close to the end (the story itself, backtracking). It felt that some of stuff were only for the extension of time.

It has a lot of similarities with Bioshock, and I was upset about it. I love to see the same mechanics, but not exact copy 1 to 1. It would be nice to have some new interesting update of them.

Also the level of difficulty was weird some time. I played on normal. But I got big groups of enemies and had to suffer a lot.

Big plus for the mechanic of tracking NPCs. I was really into investigating where is everyone and what happened with them.

The game is worth to play, but for myself I would prefer Bioshock more

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a limited variety of enemies.

citations.review_text: Super underrated. An intriguing sci-fi&horror mixture dipped in philosophy and ethics. Gameplay is great, even though there are not many types of enemies, there are *A LOT* of ways to combat them. Game lets you explore your environment and you are allowed to solve problems in various different ways (for example unlocking a door, moving and obstacle and such) and the player is rewarded for exploring. Npcs and environment feel alive and every story progression makes you wonder what is next. Unfortunately this game has its fair share of glitches and bugs but the masterpiece story makes it worth playing. Def replayable, def recommending!!!

A seriously underrated game. I first played it back when I was still in school, and at the time I couldn’t understand why it wasn’t just another DOOM. Almost ten years after its release, I finally came back to it and actually finished it and the game really opened up in a completely different way.

The graphics still hold up incredibly well, and the gameplay is probably the game’s biggest strength. There’s a surprising amount of freedom and variety in how you can approach different situations. Definitely recommend it to anyone who’s into immersive sims.

That said, I strongly recommend playing it on Nightmare with all the difficulty modifiers enabled. Otherwise, once you’ve properly leveled up, the combat can feel way too easy. The main game also suffers from a somewhat limited enemy variety, something the DLC does a much better job of addressing. It would’ve been great if some of the DLC's new enemies had been added to the main campaign as well.

It’s a shame the game didn’t sell well enough to justify a sequel, because I’d genuinely love to see more of it.
The combat isn't very good (a lack of enemy variety is where it suffers most), and I didn't like how the story was handled at all. This could have been a much better game.

citations.review_text:
An excellent atmospheric FPS with a compelling story, strong exploration, and a fantastic immersive-sim design. Thalos I is a fascinating setting, and the game gives you a huge amount of freedom in how you approach situations. Horewer, despite all its qualities, the experience becomes somewhat tedious toward the end and struggles to maintain the same level of tension throughout the entire game.

100% Completion
Time : 77H
Completion Difficulty : 7/10
Playthroughs : 3+
Missables : Yes
Guide Recommended : Yes - for collectibles
DLC required : Yes
Notable requirements : Complete the main game multiples times with the three different ability path, complete the game with all humans alive and all humans dead, various challenges.

citations.review_text:
OH my GOSH it is so good. It goes on sale for the ultimate bundle for like 8$ just pick it up.

It is well crafted and the dlc takes what you learned in the main campaign to make a fun rogue-lite mode. Only problem is that the late game is kinda easy in both the main game and dlc because you get so much good gear by the end. For the bulk of it though it is balanced just make sure you do the side quests as you get them. Also if you can avoid combat sometimes it is worth it to conserve ammo.

Easily the best hybrid RPG/Action game I've played this year.  I don't know why I waited so long.  It's just beautifully constructed, deep environmental storytelling, and every piece of the puzzle falls into place between the setting, the characters, the universe that is constructed.  I am a prolific email reader, so having those parts in helped characterize even the most modest side characters.  The fact that every NPC is named, and there are job titles and you can locate all their bodies is really a nice touch for helping to explore every inch of the map.

The gameplay itself: gunplay and puzzles and objectives are fun.  I really liked the horror elements, which a It's challenging enough for the first 60% of the game, but eventually you become powerful enough to destroy even the scariest things.  It is gameplay that naturally evolves from its narrative arc, so it feels quite appropriate given the storytelling going on.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the final act of the game experiences pacing issues, dragging or turning frustrating during the endgame.

citations.review_text:
Prey is an ambitious spiritual successor to games like System Shock and Deus Ex. The developers that worked on this project won't be getting any of your money, so as much as I'd like to support their efforts with a positive review, what's left is to warn gamers of a VERY buggy DLC and a main game that is very good for the first 2/3rds of a playthrough, and a horrible mess for the last 3rd. If you can get this game on SALE you'll have a blast for 20-30 hours, and start to question your sanity as you approach the endgame. 

The main issue with the ending parts of this game can be summarized by a level-loading system that does not at all compliment what the game asks you to do, which is quickly moving around the different levels to accomplish small errands. This will result in you watching loading screen after loading screen in between 1-2 minutes of gameplay, sandwiched with audio calls from NPCs that not only become an immersion breaking chore, but can be cut off by bugs and interrupted by gameplay without any way to return to them. The game feels really messy, but at this point in your investment you may as well get to the end of the game and move on with your life. 

The DLC would be incredible if it wasn't for extremely frequent crashes that have never been patched. Highly recommend you google "Prey Mooncrash keeps crashing" to see thread after thread of nobody having a solution. 

Ultimately, the developers did an amazing job with what resources they were given, but weren't able to support and patch the game to a fully-playable and stable product. It's a shame since this genre of game is sorely underrepresented.

I really wanted to like this game, and lots of it was great, especially the beginning. But the last third are so damn frustrating. Poor dame design, game-breaking bugs (I was stuck battling invisible walls in the scan coral nodes quest for hours, and the two endgame options are equally badly designed, there's even a section where you pretty much have to have a GLOO gun and cannisters to progress, etc.). So I could only recommend this to someone who's willing to follow online guides. I'm not normally that type of person.

For anyone saying I need to gg, I've played and completed all Fallout, Bioshock, Borderlands, Dark Souls/Elden Ring, Metal Gear Solid, Portal, etc. So it's not a question of difficulty. It's a question of bad and buggy game design. Too bad the game looks so cool.

I could never get far in either System Shock despite being a huge fan of the genre, but I've played through Prey multiple times and keep returning to it. My only real complaint is that the final act of the game drags with repetitive combat encounters, everything up until then is about the peak of freeform immersive sim games.

I want to start by saying this first - I know I'm extremely late with this review (9 years late) so I doubt anyone will really care at this point but I still want to share my opinion of Prey, in 2026.

I've had Prey since day 1. Back when I was a "newbie" to PC gaming and I know it launched with... let's just say... terrible PC optimisation which ruined my opinion of it. Sadly, It got added to my ever expanding Backlog and somewhat forgotten about due to the issues. (I wasn't sure if it was my PC or not but doing some research, it was indeed the game).

Here I am in 2026, FINALLY playing Prey to 100% completion and I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. Below I will explain why, so let's get to it!

[h1][b] What I liked/Pros [/b][/h1] 
⚫Compared to it's launch, almost all of the game's "poor" optimisation issues have been fixed. I didn't encounter a single issue. No lagging, stuttering, FPS drops, crashing e.t.c e.t.c. Nothing. Compared to 2017 and 2018.
⚫I absolutely adore how well designed Talos I is. The entire space station is interconnected. What I mean by this is - no matter where you are, you can go ANYWHERE in the station you want to go (and out). This HEAVILY encourages exploration (at your own pace too).
⚫There are so many ways to approach objectives. You can choose to go stealthy and sneak around Talos I. You can choose to go full out on Combat and kill everything (including humans). You can manipulate the environment with Typhon or Human "abilities" and so many, many other ways. It's up to you to decide how "YOU WANT TO PLAY".
⚫Prey's Atmosphere is beyond stellar (pun intended as it's in space haha). Alone on a space station (for a while), navigating some sort of... disaster? invasion? The paranoia the game makes you feel. Could that be a mimic? Could THAT be a mimic? COULD THAT BE A MIMIC?!?!?! You never know. Watch what you pick up!!
⚫About exploring - you find employee terminals that have emails, Audio logs (transcribes), employee…

Let me preface this by saying that Prey is my favourite game of all time.

Prey perfectly realises cosmic horror without making you feel helpless as a player. Its story is a grand puzzle that points you in the direction of the next puzzle piece, but lets you explore and piece it together however you want. As a new player you'll feel that your choices matter, and if you come back to play it again you'll be surprised at just how many options there are, and how things change depending on the order in which you do them.

Prey is an immersive sim. An immersive sim that presents you with problems and lets you solve them on your own, and there is an incredible number of ways to approach any given problem. There's an unpowered door? You could:
- Power the door by repairing the power junction.
- Force it open if you're strong enough.
- Use the movement system and tools at your disposal to find a way around the door. Maybe scale the wall and jump in through the ceiling?
- Something else entirely.
This is the general approach to the problems in your path in Prey, and I love it. It's not like most games where there is one or two ways to solve a problem. As long as you manage to progress, the method of doing so is almost entirely up to you.

Add to this a beatiful artstyle, satisfying and unique mechanics, and a soundtrack that pleasures me in ways I'm not allowed to recount in a steam review.

Let me list the few things I dislike about this game:
- Scripted voice lines have awful sound mixing. Set voice volume to 30% and you're good, but it does really throw you off initially.
- Zero-oxygen areas make you put on your helmet. The helmet overlay can be disorientating.
- The game has not been given the advertisment it deserves. It plays like an intelligent story-driven puzzle game but its marketing feel more like a generic space boomer shooter.

In summary, Prey is a gem that you should absolutely give a try. It's not everyone's cup of tea, but I adore it.

I thoroughly enjoyed this game as well as all others by Arkane Studios and highly recommend it as well as the Mooncrash DLC. Additionally, my friend played 50 hours and asked me to post her review in my region. Her words are posted below:

What I liked the most about Prey was its environmental design and attention to detail. Talos 1 feels like a place people actually used to live in, and everything you come across (be it weapons, materials, consumables, or dead bodies) has an in-universe reason to be there. Emails, notes and audio logs you acquire help contextualize life on the station, but they also provide valuable information that ties in with the main plot. For me, finding these pieces of lore was often the most exciting part, since they helped me form a clearer picture of the events that led to the start of the game, and fueled my speculations about where the story was going. 

Prey also has possibly the best tool for exploration I've ever seen in a game. Early on you get the GLOO cannon, which shoots a quickly solidifying gypsum-like substance that can stick to almost any surface. In addition to stunning enemies, this weapon allows you to create platforms and stairs, which in turn enables you to climb obstacles and even walls, getting to areas that may otherwise be off-limits. Traversing the station in this way feels incredibly freeing, and the developers clearly encouraged it, littering the lovingly crafted environments with secrets. 

The story in Prey is quite sparse, with the aforementioned emails and notes doing most of the work. Still, there are a couple of interesting twists and turns, and I enjoyed the world-building and the game's contemplative, philosophical tone. Prey vibes like something from the golden age of sci-fi, both in story and in atmosphere, and it scratched the itch for me as a lover of the genre, even if I wished for more from the main narrative. If you are someone who likes exploration and sci-fi stories, I highly recommend this one.

citations.review_text:
Great game, just a long learning curve. Biggest pain is the card keys, and finding them.
It's really an amazing game, if you take your time and complete all side missions. 

If it was not game of the year I would be surprised. Love it.

One of my favorite games.

Combat loop is very fun and engaging. Especially with weapon/item combos and skills.

The crafting and building component fits into the universe well and isn't too limiting or demanding.

The "puzzles" are fun, since it mostly focuses on letting you get into a room in various ways. (find the keycard on the body after checking the terminal, shoot the open door button with the nerf crossbow, turn into a coffee cup and slip through the gap under the window.)

The lore and story is neat.

The Mooncrash DLC is a fun addition. If you enjoy the combat and mechanics of the game, I would recommend it. If you enjoyed the vibe, pacing and feel of the game and want more of that, it may not be what you're looking for.
